newsitem.title: USA: Countdown begins for U.S. astronaut's return.
newsitem.headline: Countdown begins for U.S. astronaut's return.

text.p: Countdown clocks began ticking (on) Friday for the shuttle Atlantis' mission to collect Shannon Lucid from the Russian space station Mir.
Atlantis' 10-day flight, delayed more than six weeks by rocket problems, a scheduling clash and a hurricane, is due to get under way Monday with a pre-dawn blast-off from the Kennedy Space Centre.
"It looks like the third time's the charm," said shuttle commander Bill Readdy as his crew of six arrived at the Florida launch site. "Shannon is obviously looking forward to us getting up there."
U.S. Air Force meteorologists predicted a 70 percent chance of good weather for Atlantis' launch during a short seven-minute window that opens at 4:54 a.m. EDT (0854 GMT) on Monday.
Lucid, the second U.S. astronaut to live on Mir, arrived at the 10-year-old Russian space outpost in March and was supposed to return home in early August.

The 53-year-old mother of three told CNN on Thursday that her five-month stay in space had made her look younger and feel better. She explained that the weightless conditions had given her a natural face lift and she no longer has calluses on her feet.
"I told my husband not to worry. That even though we've found the fountain of youth, I'm still headed home whenever the shuttle gets here," she said.
Atlantis will also drop off Lucid's replacement, John Blaha, who is due to stay aboard Mir until January. NASA plans to staff the Russian station with U.S. astronauts into 1998.
